correctness.rationale: The Frobenius norm of a row prefix of length j is sqrt(j), and of a column prefix of length i is sqrt(i); translating the exact Heuer–Striker halfspaces gives necessary-and-sufficient ball containment. First-row length-one column prefixes and the row-total upper bound force (n+sqrt(n))r<=1 when m<=n. The constant matrix rho attains equality. Saturation forces the first row, and also the first column when m=n. Explicit small perturbation constructions strictly satisfy all other prefix inequalities and therefore prove the complete affine hull and exact universal tangent facets. The standalone 70-digit checker passed 1521 shapes 2<=m,n<=40 with 45682 labeled active inequalities; finite tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical and explicitly defined generalization of assignment polytopes. Exact Euclidean incenter *sets*, not simply a scalar radius, are natural canonical geometry: their affine dimensions rise quadratically while a change in matrix aspect ratio forces an additional family of universally tangent facets. The result resolves the full two-parameter family, supplies generic and special contact counts, and distinguishes it from the nonnegative assignment-polytope geometry; these are nontrivial structural data not directly provided as a theorem by the facet list. Its scope is intentionally limited to the standard Frobenius realization.
